files.title: About Ansible Molecule[¶](#about-ansible-molecule "Permanent link")
files.summary:
Molecule is an Ansible testing framework designed for developing and testing [Ansible](https://ansible.com) collections, playbooks, and roles.

Molecule leverages standard Ansible features including inventory, playbooks, and collections to provide flexible testing workflows.

files.title: Installation[¶](#installation "Permanent link")
files.summary:
This document assumes the developer has a basic understanding of Python packaging, and how to install and manage Python on the system executing Molecule.

## Requirements[¶](#requirements "Permanent link")

A recent version of `ansible-core` that is still under support.

Depending on the driver chosen, you may need to install additional OS packages.

CentOSUbuntu

`[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-1)$ sudo dnf install -y gcc python3-pip python3-devel openssl-devel python3-libselinux
`

`[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-1-1)$ sudo apt update
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-1-2)$ sudo apt install -y python3-pip libssl-dev
`

## Pip[¶](#pip "Permanent link")

[pip](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/installation/) is the only supported installation method.

Recommendation

The **recommended** approach to install `molecule` is using the `ansible-dev-tools` package.

files.title: Contributing[¶](#contributing "Permanent link")
files.summary:
Noticed a bug or have an idea to improve Ansible Molecule? Want to write some documentation or share your expertise on the forum? There are many ways to get involved and contribute, find out how.

## Guidelines[¶](#guidelines "Permanent link")

* We are interested in various different kinds of improvement for Molecule; please feel free to raise an [Issue](https://github.com/ansible-community/molecule/issues/new/choose)if you would like to work on something major to ensure efficient collaboration and avoid duplicate effort.
* Create a topic branch from where you want to base your work.
* Make sure you have added tests for your changes.
* Although not required, it is good to sign off commits using `git commit --signoff`, and agree that usage of `--signoff`constitutes agreement with the terms of [DCO 1.1](https://github.com/ansible-community/molecule/blob/main/DCO%5F1%5F1.md).
* Run all the tests to ensure nothing else was accidentally broken.
* Reformat the code by following the formatting section below.
* Submit a pull request.

## Talk to us[¶](#talk-to-us "Permanent link")

Connect with the Ansible community!

Join the Ansible forum to ask questions, get help, and interact with the community.

* [Get Help](https://forum.ansible.com/c/help/6): get help or help others.

files.title: Workflow Reference[¶](#workflow-reference "Permanent link")
files.summary:
This document provides a comprehensive reference for Molecule's actions, sequences, and subcommands in the ansible-native approach.

## Overview[¶](#overview "Permanent link")

When running Molecule, you must provide a **subcommand** that determines what action or sequence of actions will be executed.

`[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-1)molecule <subcommand> [options]
`

Each subcommand executes either:

* **A single action** \- Runs one specific playbook
* **A sequence** \- Runs an ordered list of actions

### Execution Flow[¶](#execution-flow "Permanent link")

**Subcommand** → **Sequence** → **Actions** → **Playbooks**

1.

files.title: Using podman containers[¶](#using-podman-containers "Permanent link")
files.summary:
Note

This example demonstrates the use of an ansible-native configuration.

This example demonstrates testing with Podman containers using standard Ansible inventory and playbooks for complete control over the testing environment.

## Overview[¶](#overview "Permanent link")

This scenario uses:

* **Inventory management**: Standard Ansible inventory files for container definitions
* **Container lifecycle**: Managed through Ansible playbooks with full customization
* **Flexible configuration**: Container settings defined in inventory for easy modification

When you run `molecule test --scenario-name podman`, Molecule executes the complete test sequence including create, converge, verify, cleanup, and destroy steps using your custom playbooks.

## Configuration[¶](#configuration "Permanent link")

The configuration uses standard Ansible patterns:

molecule.yml

`[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-1)---
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-2)ansible:
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-3)  cfg:
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-4)    defaults:
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-5)      deprecation_warnings: false
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-6)  executor:
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-7)    args:
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-8)      ansible_playbook:
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-9)        - --inventory=inventory/
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-10)
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-11)dependency:
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-12)  name: galaxy
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-13)  options:
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-14)    requirements-file: ${MOLECULE_SCENARIO_DIRECTORY}/requirements.yml
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-15)
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-16)scenario:
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-17)  test_sequence:
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-18)    - dependency
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-19)    - destroy
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-20)    - create
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-21)    - converge
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-22)    - idempotence
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-23)    - verify
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-24)    - cleanup
[](#%5F%5Fcodelineno-0-25)    - destroy
`

**Key points**: The `ansible` section configures inventory location and executor arguments.
